evidence.excerpt: Selective laser sintered (SLS) polyamide 12 specimens were subjected to 10 repeated cycles of moisture absorption (95% RH, 37 °C, 7 days) and desorption (23 °C, 50% RH, 7 days) prior to fatigue testing. A control group was tested in the dry-as-built condition. Tension–tension fatigue tests (R = 0.1, 1 Hz, 37 °C) were performed. The cyclic hygroscopic treatment reduced fatigue life at 40 MPa by 38% compared with the dry control group. Micro-CT imaging performed before and after the hygroscopic cycling revealed enlargement of interlayer porosity, with mean pore diameter increasing from 48 µm to 67 µm. Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) showed a reduction in storage modulus of 12% and an increase in the loss tangent peak area of 18% after hygroscopic cycling, indicating increased viscoelastic energy dissipation per cycle. The findings are relevant to the growing use of SLS-printed PA12 in patient-specific surgical guides and low-load orthopaedic ancillaries.
